thread:
sre-bot: PAGER: rdma-link-flap on cluster-prod-2 affecting serving pool (severity: P1) :rotating_light:
ryan_infra: I'm seeing a spike in IB packet retransmits and a handful of nodes reporting 'mlx5 QP error' around 21:10 UTC. Lots of resends.
nisha_serving: Customers hitting 503s for gen and chat endpoints. Error spike correlates with same timeframe. Investigating serving logs now.
tom_runtime: A few containers crashed with: `Cuda error: out of memory` immediately after RDMA retransmit bursts. Stack traces show failure while compacting KV cache.
jamie_ops: paging @leah_oncall and @ryan_infra — can you confirm which nodes? I'm pulling node list.
leah_oncall: Oncall here. Node list: prod-gpu-12, prod-gpu-13, prod-gpu-14. prod-gpu-13 shows netlink flaps, `ibdev0` resets.
ryan_infra: Running `rdma link show` on prod-gpu-13:
```
# rdma link show
dev: mlx5_0 state: ACTIVE (1)
port 1: mtu 4096, state ACTIVE
port 2: mtu 4096, state DOWN
log: pkey violation? rx_pkt_drops=12456 tx_retries=320
```
leah_oncall: Also seeing kernel logs: `mlx5_core 0000:af:00.1: pkey violation, sending NAK` and then `mlx5_ib_poll_cq: poll CQ err -110` repeated.
jamie_ops: Noted. Quick mitigation options: 1) cordon problematic nodes, 2) failover traffic to TCP-only pool, 3) reduce batch sizes/prefetch to lower memory pressure. Thoughts?
nisha_serving: We can flip runtime fallback to TCP for affected customers in ~30s. Will also lower max_batch_size to 1 for riskier models. Command I plan to run: `redwoodctl config set serving.fallback_network=TCP --scope=cluster-prod-2 --reason "rdma flaps"`
ryan_infra: Good. I'm going to cordon prod-gpu-13 and drain pods gracefully: `kubectl cordon prod-gpu-13 && kubectl drain prod-gpu-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
tom_runtime: Adding to that — will push a runtime override to reduce model KV cache retention: `runtimectl set kv_cache_retention=low --pool=gpu-12-14` to avoid OOMs during retries.
leah_oncall: Executed cordon+drain on prod-gpu-13. Pod eviction in progress. Some pods restarted on prod-gpu-12 and prod-gpu-14.
customer-success: We're seeing two high-revenue customers (acct: ACME, acct: Skylark) hit degraded latency and some 503s. Communicating to leads, will send interim note after we stabilize.
ryan_infra: For prod-gpu-12 I'm seeing intermittent hardware link down events on port 2. Opening ticket with datacenter: `DC ticket #DC-7891: IB link resets on host prod-gpu-12/13` and attaching logs.
jamie_ops: Can we route traffic to dedicated TCP pool while infra investigates? If we enable TCP fallback at edge, should be seamless albeit higher latency/cost.
nisha_serving: Done: `redwoodctl rollout set-route-fallback --route=gen,chat --fallback=TCP --duration=30m` — rolling to 100% for cluster-prod-2. Watching for errors.
sre-bot: ACTIONS: cordon prod-gpu-13, drain in progress; set route fallback TCP; lowered batch sizes; KV cache retention reduced. Oncall: leah_oncall. Incident lead: ryan_infra.
leah_oncall: After fallback enabled, 503s dropped by ~85%, some customers still see higher latencies but error rate is down. Monitoring traces now.
tom_runtime: We still see a few CUDA OOM logs on nodes that recovered pods quickly — likely from retries during retransmit storms. On longer term, we should add graceful backoff on reconnect and limit concurrency per-gpu.
ryan_infra: DC responded: observed flaps on top-of-rack IB switch affecting two adjacent hosts; replaced SFPs on switch, but link still unstable. They recommend moving affected VMs off hardware until full switch replacement.
jamie_ops: Next mitigation: move workloads off hosts (taint + migrate) and scale up TCP-only pool to absorb baseline traffic. Starting scale-up now: `redwoodctl pool scale tcp-prod-2 --delta=+8`
customer-success: Notifying ACME/SKYLARK with status update: "We've mitigated the main error vector by routing traffic to TCP, and are migrating workloads off affected hosts. Expect latency degradation ~+100-300ms for 30-60 minutes."
leah_oncall: Hands off to night SRE at 23:00 UTC. I'll prepare handoff summary: incident start 21:10 UTC, primary vector: IB link flaps -> packetloss -> retransmits -> container OOMs -> crashes. Mitigations applied: cordon+drain prod-gpu-13, TCP fallback for gen/chat, batch size and KV cache reductions, scaling TCP pool, DC ticket opened.
ryan_infra: Opening incident incident tracker: `INC-2026-1834`. Assigning follow-ups: hardware replacement (DC), postmortem (oncall + eng-runtime + infra), add runtime throttles & backoff.
tom_runtime: Quick config note for post-incident: consider defaulting fallback to TCP when retransmit rate > X and add a circuit-breaker to pause aggressive batching when network errors spike.
sre-bot: Reminder: Pager duty may still trigger until drained nodes are out of rotation and all error rates below threshold for 15m.
leah_oncall: Last check before handoff: error rate 503s down to 0.7% (from 12%), latency p95 up +180ms. Keeping pages for hardware replacement ticket. Handoff to @jamie_ops for overnight watch.
jamie_ops: On it. Will keep the TCP fallback for 6 hours, schedule a staged failback after switch replacement and thorough validation. Logging postmortem owners: @tom_runtime (runtime), @ryan_infra (infra), @nisha_serving (product impact).
customer-success: ACME & Skylark acknowledged. They asked for more detail about failover timeline; will coordinate with PMs.
sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations active; status = stabilizing; next update in 30m or on change. :white_check_mark:
